# @sharadox/scroll-web-library

> Smooth scrolling (Lenis) and active-section tracking for React.

- /smooth-scroll: <SmoothScroll duration=1.15 anchorOffset=-60 /> — off with prefers-reduced-motion; handles a[href^="#"] clicks
- /active-section: useActiveSection(ids: readonly string[]) → { active: id at viewport middle, within: 0–1 through it, page: 0–1 page progress }
- Peer: react. License: Sharadox Open Source License 0.1.0
- SmoothScroll works in a page or a layout (it starts afresh for every pathname). Each page's smoothing stops the moment the address is another page's (link, back or forward) and a new page stops the previous one's, so a glide or trackpad momentum from the old page never moves the new one; for 300 ms after a page opens, wheel and touch are left to the browser while Next.js places it (0.4.2).
- SmoothScroll also turns plain clicks on links to the current page (same path, no hash or query, no target, no modifier keys) into a scroll to the top, without reloading — with or without reduced motion.
- /glide: glideTo(top, { duration? }) — through the running SmoothScroll (Lenis) or window.scrollTo (smooth, or auto with reduced motion); registerGlider is internal to SmoothScroll
- /glide-into-view: glideIntoView(element, { offset? = 96, duration? }) — glides the element's top to offset below the window's top, only when it isn't wholly in view (0.5.0)
- /scroll-steps: useScrollSteps(sectionRef, count, { duration? = 0.9 }) — while the section is pinned, each wheel gesture (a pause of 180 ms starts a new one) or finger swipe (30 px+) glides exactly one step; step i sits at top + (i + 0.5) / count × (height − innerHeight); past the ends the page scrolls on
- 0.3.0: glide, scroll-steps
- 0.3.1: a finger swipe's step glide starts after the touch event, so smooth scrolling (Lenis) no longer stops it on phones
- /section-link: <SectionLink href …LinkProps> — next/link; for "#id" on this page scroll={false} (SmoothScroll glides), for "/path#id" Next.js navigates and scrolls as usual; SmoothScroll glides (or, with reduced motion, jumps) to the anchor even though Link took the click
- 0.4.0: SectionLink; SmoothScroll handles "#top" (top of the open page) and anchors whose click a Next.js Link already took; next is a peer dependency
- 0.4.1: SectionLink leaves Next.js scrolling on for sections of other pages ("/en#contact"), so they land on the section
